questions.prompt: For a candidate V(x) > 0, the derivative along trajectories V-dot is negative for all x in a ball |x| < r (x not zero). What can you conclude?
options: The origin is asymptotically stable, with a sublevel set of V inside the ball as a region of attraction
The origin is unstable outside the ball and so unstable overall, because V-dot is unknown there
Nothing can be concluded unless V-dot is negative on the whole state space, not just a ball
The origin is globally asymptotically stable, since V decreases along every trajectory in the ball
questions.explanation: Local Lyapunov theorem: a sublevel set of V inside the ball is invariant. Global stability would need V-dot < 0 everywhere and V radially unbounded.
questions.skillLabel: Basin of attraction and local versus global

questions.prompt: A damped pendulum's energy has V-dot = -b*omega^2 (zero whenever omega = 0). Why can we still conclude the hanging equilibrium is asymptotically stable?
options: Because V-dot = 0 means V is constant forever, and so the pendulum must come to rest by itself
We cannot conclude it; only Lyapunov stability holds whenever V-dot is merely negative semidefinite
LaSalle: the only invariant set where omega = 0 is the bottom, so trajectories converge to it
Because -b*omega^2 is strictly negative at every state, so V decreases at all times everywhere
questions.explanation: If omega stays 0 then theta'' = 0 forces sin(theta) = 0; only the bottom is invariant.

questions.prompt: Inverted pendulum theta'' = g_l*sin(theta) + a with g_l = 9.81 and a torque limit |a| <= 6. What is the largest angle (rad, 3 decimals) at which gravity can still be cancelled (a >= g_l sin(theta))?
